minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard school COVID grant update and a town manager plan for special town meeting, with a Chapter 90 tracked-vehicle purchase questioned.
minutes.summary: The school business manager and superintendent presented COVID-related spending, federal and state grants, open positions and possible surpluses, and the committee asked about grant-funded positions, Chromebooks, live-streaming technology, and bus contract language. The town manager reviewed adjustments to the FY21 budget and the deferred capital projects for the special town meeting, and the committee pressed her on buying a piece of equipment with Chapter 90 funds. A tax increment financing proposal for a greenhouse company was discussed, and the committee approved two sets of minutes by roll call and adjourned.

public_comment.topic: Cautioned against using Chapter 90 money for things other than roads, asked whether the Chromebooks could be covered by COVID grants, and asked what COVID-related unemployment costs are.

what_happened.line: The committee questioned the town manager on buying a tracked vehicle with Chapter 90 funds, which was left out of the deferred capital projects returning to the special town meeting.
The school business manager and superintendent reviewed COVID-related spending, federal and state grants, open positions and possible surpluses for FY20 and FY21.
The town manager reviewed FY21 budget adjustments: new growth above the town meeting estimate, health insurance savings, and added COVID costs for the second half of the year.
The town accountant agreed to provide a schedule of all special revenue fund balances as of the close of FY20.
The committee approved two sets of minutes by roll call and set next week's meeting as the public hearing on special town meeting warrant articles.

why_it_matters: Chapter 90 money is state road aid, so using it for equipment outside road work changes what is left for roads and is a question residents may be asked about at the special town meeting.
Several school positions rest on grants that expire, so when they end it is a loss of grant money, not a cut to the local school budget, and the town would face a choice about replacing them.
watch_next: Public hearing on the special town meeting warrant articles next week, with article-by-article recommendations.
